title: Treat obesity with an approved oral small-molecule GLP-1 agonist

concept.text: Deliver clinically effective incretin-based weight management through a non-peptide oral drug. Orforglipron achieved approval, separating this milestone from oral delivery of peptide semaglutide. Proposed completion test: FDA chronic weight-management approval for an orally administered non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist, supported by randomized phase 3 weight-loss trials lasting approximately 72 weeks. Test set by: FDA; the approved indication covers adults with obesity or overweight and at least one weight-related comorbidity. Reported achieved: FDA approved orforglipron (Foundayo) on 1 April 2026. Overlaps: END-05, PHA-11. Sources given: [FDA Foundayo approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-new-molecular-entity-under-national-priority-voucher-program?source=tmtc) ; [FDA Foundayo prescribing information](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/220934Orig1s000lbl.pdf).

page.title: First oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist for obesity
page.definition: An FDA-approved oral nonpeptide drug activates the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor, the target of a gut hormone that regulates appetite and insulin secretion. It reduces excess body weight and maintains weight reduction long term in adults with obesity.

goal.need: In 2024, 940 million adults worldwide were living with obesity. FDA's weight-reduction guidance cites improvements in metabolic and cardiovascular risk factors with sustained losses of at least 5% of baseline weight for some interventions. An oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist provides a drug treatment without injections.

figures.caption: Worldwide adult overweight and obesity in 2024
figures.note: The obesity population is included in the overweight total.

statements.quote: with a goal of reduced morbidity and mortality.
statements.context: FDA's January 2025 draft guidance defines weight reduction as a long-term reduction in excess body fat. The guidance contains nonbinding recommendations.

statements.quote: Lilly is investigating orforglipron, its first nonpeptide oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, for chronic weight management in the ATTAIN phase 3 clinical program

completion.title: FDA approves an oral non-peptide small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist for long-term weight reduction.
completion.criterion: The US Food and Drug Administration approves an orally administered GLP-1 receptor agonist that is a non-peptide small molecule, such as orforglipron (molecular weight of its calcium salt 902.0 g/mol), to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity, or with overweight and at least one weight-related comorbid condition, with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. Oral semaglutide, a peptide, does not count. The first such approval was Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets, once daily, on 1 April 2026, supported by two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of 72 weeks; ATTAIN-1 randomized 3,127 adults without diabetes.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, NDA 220934 approval letter, Foundayo prescribing information and news release of 1 April 2026.
completion.threshold_quote: provides for the use of Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long term in adults with obesity or adults with overweight in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition.
completion.basis: Checked on 15 November 2026 against the FDA approval letter, signed 1 April 2026, the prescribing information and the FDA news release of that day. FDA documents call orforglipron a GLP-1 receptor agonist and give its formula; the pivotal trial report calls it an oral small-molecule agonist. The test is the first approval of this form of drug, not a weight-loss figure: mean loss in ATTAIN-1 was 11.2% at the highest dose. The trials used capsules; a bioequivalence study links the 36-mg capsule to the 17.2-mg tablet.

milestones.title: An oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist reduces primate food intake at one-sided P < 0.025.
milestones.criterion: Oral dosing reduces mean food consumption versus vehicle during 90-minute feeding periods over 5 days of daily treatment in cynomolgus monkeys, using multiplicity-adjusted Dunnett comparisons at one-sided α=0.025. This is the published orforglipron experiment's test. Kawai et al. reported it in 2020: 8 monkeys in a crossover experiment received 0.05 or 0.1 mg/kg daily; food consumption decreased, with reported comparisons reaching P<0.005.
milestones.set_by: Chugai and Eli Lilly investigators, Kawai et al., published food-consumption experiment and statistical analysis; this protocol is specific to orforglipron.
milestones.threshold_quote: by one-sided significance level of 2.5% for the order of increase (insulin) or decrease (glucose, mean food consumption)

milestones.title: An oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist advances to repeated human dosing after a protocol safety review.
milestones.criterion: The registered phase 1 protocol starts repeated oral dosing after reviewing safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetic (drug exposure) and pharmacodynamic (biological response) data through day 5 of the third single-dose cohort. NCT03929744 administered single doses to 32 participants and repeated doses to 60 participants between 12 June 2019 and 2 November 2020. Repeated dosing lasted 4 weeks, reaching 24 mg/day; no deaths or serious adverse events occurred.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, NCT03929744 phase 1 protocol, procedures published by Pratt et al.; the progression decision is specific to orforglipron.
milestones.threshold_quote: after review of the safety, tolerability and available PK and PD data collected up to Day 5 of the third SAD level.

milestones.title: An oral nonpeptide GLP-1 agonist beats placebo for weight reduction at 26 weeks in phase 2.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate superiority to placebo on the prespecified mean percentage change in body weight at week 26 in a randomized phase 2 study. NCT05051579 randomized 272 adults without diabetes to oral orforglipron capsules, 12–45 mg/day, or placebo. Published on 23 June 2023, mean weight reductions at week 26 were 8.6–12.6% with orforglipron versus 2.0% with placebo. The efficacy analysis estimated outcomes assuming treatment continuation; it did not adjust for multiple comparisons.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, NCT05051579 phase 2 protocol and statistical analysis, published by Wharton et al.; the endpoint and duration are specific to orforglipron.
milestones.threshold_quote: testing the superiority of orforglipron as compared with placebo with respect to the primary end point.

milestones.title: An oral GLP-1 agonist beats control weight loss by ≥5 percentage points after 1 year at maintenance dose.
milestones.criterion: After at least 1 year at maintenance dosage, mean percentage weight reduction exceeds control by ≥5 percentage points, with statistical significance. This is FDA's nonbinding draft recommendation. ATTAIN-1 randomized 3,127 adults without diabetes for 72 weeks, including 52 weeks at the 36-mg capsule maintenance dose. Published on 16 September 2025, weight loss was 11.2% at 36 mg/day versus 2.1% with placebo: a 9.1-point difference (95% CI 8.1–10.1; P<0.001), estimated regardless of treatment discontinuation.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, January 2025 draft guidance, section III.B.3.c, Efficacy benchmarks; the recommendation covers weight-reduction drugs generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: is at least 5% and the difference is statistically significant.

results.finding: Oral LY3502970 reduced food consumption versus vehicle in 8 cynomolgus monkeys, with one-sided Dunnett comparisons reaching P<0.005.
results.detail: An 8 × 5 crossover study tested 0.05 and 0.1 mg/kg daily for 5 days, measuring food consumption during 90-minute feeding periods. Dunnett comparisons adjusted for multiplicity at one-sided α=0.025.
results.quote: LY3502970 at 0.05 and 0.1 mg/kg decreased food consumption from the first to the fifth days of dosing in a dose-dependent manner

results.finding: Oral orforglipron in 272 randomized adults produced up to 10.6 percentage points greater mean weight reduction than placebo at week 26.
results.detail: Randomized phase 2 trial in adults without diabetes; week 26 was the prespecified primary endpoint. The efficacy estimand assumed treatment continuation. No multiplicity adjustment was applied.
results.quote:
At week 26, the mean 
change from baseline in body weight ranged from −8.6% to −12.6% across the 
orforglipron dose cohorts and was −2.0% in the placebo group.

results.finding: Oral orforglipron in 272 randomized adults produced up to 12.3 percentage points greater mean weight reduction than placebo at week 36.
results.detail: The weight-loss difference exceeded the numerical threshold, but treatment lasted only 36 weeks, including up to 16 weeks of dose escalation. This does not establish efficacy after at least one year at maintenance dosage.
results.quote:
Weight reduction continued through week 36, 
with the placebo-corrected percentage change 
from baseline in body weight ranging from −7.1% 
to −12.3% in the efficacy estimand.

results.finding: In ATTAIN-1 (3127 adults), oral orforglipron produced 9.1 percentage points greater mean weight reduction than placebo.
results.detail: At 36 mg/day, maintenance dosing lasted 52 weeks within the 72-week trial. The treatment-regimen estimand included outcomes regardless of treatment discontinuation; the difference was statistically significant (P<0.001; 95% CI, 8.1–10.1 percentage points).
results.quote:
and −9.1 percentage points (95% 
CI, −10.1 to −8.1) with orforglipron 36 mg 
(P<0.001 for all doses).

results.finding: Oral LY3502970 reduced food consumption versus vehicle in 8 cynomolgus monkeys (multiplicity-adjusted, one-sided Dunnett P<0.005).
results.detail: An 8 × 5 crossover study measured 90-minute food consumption during 5 days of daily oral treatment at 0.05 or 0.1 mg/kg. Dunnett comparisons adjusted for multiplicity used one-sided α=0.025.
results.quote: LY3502970 at 0.05 and 0.1 mg/kg decreased food consumption from the first to the fifth days of dosing in a dose-dependent manner ( Fig. 5 F ), similar to that observed for 0.3 and 0.6 µg/kg of exenatide ( Fig. 5 G ).

results.finding: FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets on 1 April 2026 for long-term weight reduction in adults; sample size not reported.
results.detail: Approved with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for adults with obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbid condition.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective

labeling.
